vanasadam_centre_about.title: About the Centre
vanasadam_centre_about.note: The physical Seafarers' Centre (Estonian Seamen's Mission) is at Muuga, 17 km from here — too far to walk. But Vanasadam sits right in central Tallinn, so the whole city is about 5 minutes on foot instead. Closed 25 Dec, 1 Jan, and Easter Sunday.

groups.label: Welfare services
items: Help carrying purchases from the city
Transfer to shopping centres on request

vanasadam_centre_services.note: No hot lunch is cooked — snacks and coffee are free or €1–3. This describes the Muuga centre itself; from Vanasadam it's the city on foot, not this centre.

vanasadam_centre_shuttle.title: Free Shuttle Bus
vanasadam_centre_shuttle.from: Straight from your gangway, or from the Terminal A / Terminal D checkpoint

directions.title: How to recognise it
directions.sub: White minibus (VW Transporter / Mercedes Vito), Estonian Seamen's Mission logo or a "Seamen's Club" sign on the windscreen

directions.title: No fixed timetable from Vanasadam
directions.sub: Runs on call · return time agreed with the driver on the spot

vanasadam_centre_shuttle.note: For cargo or repair vessels berthed at Vanasadam specifically — this isn't a scheduled run like some ports, so book ahead rather than just waiting at a stop.

directions.title: Book the shuttle ahead
directions.sub: See Free Shuttle Bus above — the only realistic way to reach the centre building from Vanasadam

directions.sub: From Terminal A or D, follow the lit pavement along Sadama or Kai street towards Nautica mall / the Old Town — fully paved and safe

vanasadam_centre_location.note: At night, avoid unlit construction areas around the port and unmarked vehicle exits from the ferry lanes.

vanasadam_transport_leaving.title: Leaving the Port

callout.text: Yes — shore leave is normally permitted at Vanasadam. Always confirm with your Master or ship's agent before you go: rules can change per berth and per vessel.

sections.title: If you're not from the EU / Schengen area

rows.title: Border check applies at the checkpoint
rows.sub: No Schengen visa? You'll need a Shore Leave Pass, arranged by your ship's agent in advance

rows.title: No special gear needed inside Terminals A / D
rows.sub: The passenger terminal areas are fine on foot as you are

rows.title: Hi-vis vest + safety shoes required in cargo/ISPS zones
rows.sub: If you're moving through the working cargo or repair berths

rows.title: Stay on marked walkways
rows.sub: Loading/unloading berths, ferry marshalling areas and technical roads are off-limits — follow the green/yellow marked paths only

vanasadam_transport_leaving.note: If the checkpoint turns you back, call your ship's agent, or the Seamen's Mission chaplain on duty: +372 56 462 825 (especially if a shuttle was already booked). Pedestrian zones normally run about 06:00–22:30/23:00; overnight, access goes through the security duty checkpoint.

vanasadam_transport_taxi.title: Taxi

rows.title: Bolt
rows.sub: Most common here · card payment in-app

rows.title: Uber
rows.sub: Also available in Tallinn

rows.title: Forus
rows.sub: Local Estonian app

rows.title: Official taxi ranks
rows.sub: Right at the Terminal A and Terminal D exits

vanasadam_transport_taxi.note: Typical fare into town is €5–8 through an app. Unofficial drivers sometimes wait right at the pedestrian exit offering "fast taxi" at inflated prices — a genuine taxi always has a roof sign, a price list on the right rear window and a running meter. Without those, walk on: at the terminal "first line" without an app, fares of €20–30 for a 2 km ride are not unheard of. Order through Bolt.

vanasadam_transport_public.note: About 5–8 minutes to the city centre, €2.00 for an hourly ticket. Last services run roughly 23:30–00:00 — after that, use an app taxi. No shuttle exists inside the port itself: the passenger terminals are compact enough to walk, and for the more distant repair-vessel berths, your agent or the Seamen's Mission shuttle arranges the transfer.

callout.text: Never exchange money on the street, even for a good rate someone offers you. In some countries this is a criminal offence — and it's one of the most common ways seafarers get scammed near a port.

rows.title: A stranger offers you a better rate
rows.sub: On the street, at the gate, or "just around the corner" — always a scam

rows.title: Being asked to go somewhere private
rows.sub: A car, a back room, an alley — a legitimate exchange never needs this

rows.title: No receipt offered
rows.sub: A real exchange always gives you a printed receipt with the rate used

rows.title: Know the rough official rate first
rows.sub: Check on your phone before you go — so you can spot a bad deal immediately

rows.title: Count what you receive, before you walk away
rows.sub: In front of the person who gave it to you, not after

callout.text: Before you leave, agree your return time with the ship and mark your ship's position on the Ship screen. Finding the right gate again after dark is the single most common problem ashore.

wellness_zone_vanasadam.title: Wellness Recovery Zone — Tallinn
wellness_zone_vanasadam.note: Your quiet harbor to rest, recover, and reset. A comfortable space offering massage, soothing scents, and deep relaxation for body and mind — everything you need to recharge your physical and emotional strength between watches.
